sections.h2: Which office bills property tax in Pearland, TX?
sections.html:
Your parcel's county decides. Pearland spreads across Brazoria County and Fort Bend County, and the Texas Comptroller's directory lists the City of Pearland as an active taxing unit in both appraisal districts.

Brazoria County's tax office, at 451 N. Velasco St. in Angleton, lists the City of Pearland and Pearland ISD among the units it collects for. Its phone number is 979-864-1320. The Brazoria Central Appraisal District, which sets values, is at 500 N. Chenango St. in Angleton and answers at 979-849-7792. For a Fort Bend County address, the Fort Bend Central Appraisal District is at 2801 B.F. Terry Blvd. in Rosenberg, 281-344-8623. Fort Bend County's own collection list does not include Pearland, so ask where a Fort Bend-side parcel pays.

Expect more than the city and school lines on a bill. The Brazoria list includes Pearland Municipal Management District #2, Alvin Community College District, Brazoria County emergency districts, drainage districts and dozens of numbered municipal utility districts. A newer subdivision often carries a utility district charge that an older one does not.

Schools differ by address too. Brazoria County's list includes Pearland ISD, Alvin ISD and Friendswood ISD, so the school line on your own bill shows which district charges your street.

sections.h2: What did Pearland's 2026 tax rate notice say?
sections.html:
In its 2026 notice the city lists $0.637892 as the no-new-revenue rate and $0.693542 as the voter-approval rate, both per $100 of value. The lower figure would collect the same total as last year from property taxed in both years. The higher one is, in most cases, the most a city may adopt without calling an election.

sections.h2: What dates matter for Pearland property owners each year?
sections.html:
Every Texas taxing unit works from a single statewide calendar, and the anchor is New Year's Day: the property's value, and the person who owns it, are frozen as of January 1 for that tax year.

  • January 1: value is set, and that year's lien takes hold.
  • April 1 or soon after: appraisal notices go out for single-family homesteads. Other property follows around May 1.
  • Before May 1: apply for most exemptions.
  • May 15 (or the 30th day after delivery of the notice, if that is later): last day to protest.
  • July 25: the appraisal roll is certified and sent to every taxing unit.
  • September 29 or thereabouts: last day for units to adopt rates.
  • October: bills are mailed. Tax is due by January 31 and delinquent February 1.

A late account picks up six percent in penalty and one percent in interest on the first day of February. After that the penalty gains a point per month until July 1, when it sits at 12 percent, while interest goes on at a point a month. A lawyer's collection fee of up to 20 percent is possible where the unit has such a contract.

Protest hearings before the appraisal review board begin around May 15, and the board is expected to approve the records by July 20 unless more than five percent of total value is still under protest. Save the envelope or delivery record for the appraisal notice, since a late delivery moves your protest deadline.

sections.h2: How do Pearland homeowners reduce the bill?
sections.html:
File for the homestead exemption in the first year you live in the house as your main home. The school district takes $140,000 off the value for its own tax, and a homeowner who is 65 or older or disabled gets $60,000 further. City and county governments can adopt a percentage exemption of their own, up to 20 percent of value with a $5,000 minimum. Ask Pearland whether it has, since the Brazoria directory lists the units without their exemption choices.

A homestead also gets a growth brake. Beginning the January after the exemption is first granted, its appraised value may not climb by more than 10 percent per year. Seniors and disabled owners can additionally hold their school tax at a ceiling that travels with them to a new Texas homestead.

Disabled veterans may exempt part of one property they own. The Comptroller's scale by VA disability rating runs like this:

  • Rating of 10 to 29 percent: a deduction as high as $5,000
  • Rating of 30 to 49 percent: as high as $7,500
  • Rating of 50 to 69 percent: as high as $10,000
  • Rating of 70 to 100 percent: as high as $12,000

Veterans with a 100 percent rating are fully exempt on the residence homestead. Someone who inherited a Pearland house but is not named on a recorded deed can still apply by giving the appraisal district an ownership affidavit, the death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation.

sections.h2: What if I sell a Pearland house with unpaid taxes?
sections.html:
Back tax follows the lot rather than the seller. The lien starts each January 1, delinquent amounts block clear title for a buyer, and whoever held the house on that date can still be sued for that year's bill after selling.

Penalty and interest can be waived in many cases when the tax is paid by the 21st day after the owner learns of the delinquency and a written request arrives before day 181. Residence homestead owners can ask for a payment plan, and some collectors stretch it to 36 months. Someone who appeals an appraisal must still pay the undisputed amount before the delinquency date.

After a suit and sale, a homestead can be bought back for two years once the purchaser's deed is filed, and other land for 180 days. Surplus proceeds stay claimable by the former owner for two years.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Pearland?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counted 91,252 Pearland residents in 2010 and 125,828 in 2020, and estimates 129,930 for July 2025. Land area is 48.67 square miles, which made the 2020 density about 2,585 per square mile.

Homeowners make up 76.2 percent of the 44,410 households counted for 2020-2024. A middle-of-the-range owned home is worth $356,300, and the median household brings in $118,842. Mortgage holders spend $2,611 a month at the median, renters pay $1,860, and a typical worker spends 32.7 minutes commuting. Nearly half of adults hold at least a bachelor's degree, at 47.1 percent.

faqs.q: Is Pearland in Brazoria County or Fort Bend County?
faqs.a: Both. The Comptroller's directories list the City of Pearland as a taxing unit in the Brazoria and the Fort Bend appraisal districts, so your parcel's location decides which district appraises it.

faqs.q: When is Pearland property tax delinquent?
faqs.a: Anything unpaid after January 31 becomes delinquent on February 1, the day penalty and interest start. By the first of July the penalty stands at 12 percent.

faqs.q: What rate does Pearland charge for 2026?
faqs.a: The 2026 notice shows two benchmark figures, $0.637892 and $0.693542, and no adopted rate. Your bill or the city finance office will show the rate actually set.

faqs.q: Can I pay Pearland property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. Any owner may pay half by the end of November and half by the end of June. A homestead owner who is 65 or older or disabled may use four installments, and a homestead owner who is behind may request a plan lasting as long as 36 months.

faqs.q: Who owes the current year's tax after a Pearland sale?
faqs.a: The person who owned on January 1 carries the legal liability for that year. Closings usually prorate the year between buyer and seller and clear earlier delinquent years from the proceeds.
